To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biological activity and carcinogenic effects of progastrins and Ggly in the colorectal epithelium are dependent on the presence, in the epithelium, of ferric ions.
the proliferation of the colorectal mucosal cells is stimulated by gastrin precursory peptides and that iron is required for this stimulatory action.
the proliferation-stimulatory effects of gastrins in vivo are dependent on the presence, and blocked by the removal, of iron.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the peptide hormone, gastrin, in the development of human colorectal carcinoma.
the biological activity of gastrin precursers and their role in the development of gastrointestinal cancer.
the role of iron in the pathogenesis of colorectal carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gastrin precursors are biologically active in vivo, and that this biological activity is dependent on the availability of iron.

the biological activity (proliferation) of Ggly and progastrin in the colorectum in vivo is dependent upon the presence of iron and that chelating iron from the colorectum may be of therapeutic benefit in the prevention of colorectal carcinoma.
gastrin and its precursors stimulate proliferation in colorectal epithelium, and the biological effects of these peptides require the presence of iron.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
iron is required for gastrin precursors to promote colorectal carcinogenesis.
iron is required for the biological activity of gastrin precursers in vivo, and chelating agents block the stimulatory effect of gastrin precusors in the colorectal epithelium.

the biological activity in the colorectal tract of the precursors of gastrin is dependent on the availability of iron and that chelating iron may be a novel approach to the prevention of colorectal carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

iron may be a key component of the biological activity of Ggly in vivo and that the iron chelating agent DFO may have potential as a chemopreventive agent in the development of gastrointestinal cancers.

the biological activity in vivo of the progastrin-Gly-extended gastrin system is dependent on the availability of iron, and this finding has implications for the treatment of patients with gastrointestinal tumors.
iron is essential for the biological activity of gastrin precusors in vivo.
